To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the adsorption of chlorfervinphos and of methidathion was significantly influenced by the cations in the clay and that the adsorption extent was greater in the clay with a higher cation exchange capacity (CEC).
the adsorption of chlorfervinphos and of methidathion on H+, Ca+, Na+ and K+saturated clays is influenced by the nature of the cation and the clay mineral.
the cation saturation in clays affects the adsorption of organophosphates and that adsorption of organo‐phosphates on kaolinite is less than on bentonite.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of saturating cations on the adsorption of chlorfvinphos and methiodathion in three clays.
the adsorption of organophosphorus pesticides from aqueous solutions on bentonite and kaolinite.
the influence of the saturating cations on the adsorption of chlorfensulphuron and chlorfenvinphas on the clay minerals, kaolinite and bentonite.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
adsorption is influenced by the nature of both the adsorbed and adsorbing phases.
the adsorptive behavior of the organophosphorus insecticides on the clays studied is dependent on the nature of the saturating cations.
the adsorption of chlorfervinphos and the methidathion are influenced by the nature and concentration of the cations saturating the clays, and that the adsorption isotherms are of a Freundlich‐type.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the extent and speed of adsorption of the two insecticides on the clay is related to their chemical structure, their solubility in water, and the type of clay.
adsorption on clay minerals is influenced by the saturating cations and the nature of the clay mineral.

the adsorption extent of chlorfenvinephos and methiodathion on the clay minerals is in the following sequence : H+ > Ca++ > K+ > Na+, and the adsorption of chlorfenevinphos is greater than that of methiodathion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the adsorption extent and adsorption kinetics of organophosphates are influenced by the nature of the cations saturating the clays.
the adsorption isotherms are not linear.
the adsorption of chlorfenevinphos and methadathion on the clay is influenced by the cations in the soil.
